I grouped each attorney under their most frequent visa type, counting distinct cases, and included attorneys with at least five cases. Since the database doesn’t define a specialization score, I used a Herfindahl-style score: **100 × the sum of squared shares across visa types**. The main-visa percentage is the share belonging to the attorney’s most frequent visa type.

| Category | Attorneys | Avg. specialization score | Avg. cases in main visa type (%) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| H-1B | 21 | 96.11 | 97.70 |

```sql
WITH attorney_visa AS (
  SELECT
    ca.counselmail AS attorney,
    c.visacls AS visa_type,
    COUNT(DISTINCT ca.docketkey) AS visa_cases
  FROM case_attorney AS ca
  JOIN cases AS c
    ON c.filekey = ca.docketkey
  GROUP BY ca.counselmail, c.visacls
),
attorney_totals AS (
  SELECT
    attorney,
    SUM(visa_cases) AS total_cases
  FROM attorney_visa
  GROUP BY attorney
  HAVING SUM(visa_cases) >= 5
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT
    av.attorney,
    av.visa_type,
    av.visa_cases,
    totals.total_cases,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY av.attorney
      ORDER BY av.visa_cases DESC, av.visa_type
    ) AS rn,
    100.0 * SUM(
      POWER(av.visa_cases::DOUBLE / totals.total_cases, 2)
    ) OVER (PARTITION BY av.attorney) AS specialization_score
  FROM attorney_visa AS av
  JOIN attorney_totals AS totals USING (attorney)
),
attorney_summary AS (
  SELECT
    attorney,
    visa_type AS category_name,
    specialization_score,
    100.0 * visa_cases / total_cases AS main_visa_percentage
  FROM ranked
  WHERE rn = 1
)
SELECT
  category_name,
  COUNT(*) AS attorney_count,
  CAST(ROUND(AVG(specialization_score), 2) AS DECIMAL(10, 2))
    AS avg_specialization_score,
  CAST(ROUND(AVG(main_visa_percentage), 2) AS DECIMAL(10, 2))
    AS avg_main_visa_case_percentage
FROM attorney_summary
GROUP BY category_name
ORDER BY attorney_count DESC, category_name;
```

```sql
WITH comparable_cases AS (
    SELECT
        c.filekey,
        c.jobtag AS job_title,
        TRY_CAST(
            REPLACE(REPLACE((pw.wage_details->'offered_wage'->>'from'), '$', ''), ',', '')
            AS DOUBLE
        ) AS offered_pay,
        TRY_CAST(
            REPLACE(REPLACE((pw.wage_details->'prevailing_wage'->>'value'), 'USD', ''), ',', '')
            AS DOUBLE
        ) AS prevailing_pay
    FROM cases AS c
    JOIN case_worksite AS cw
        ON cw.dockkey = c.filekey
    JOIN prevailing_wage AS pw
        ON pw.trackno = cw.wagetrack
    WHERE (pw.wage_details->'offered_wage'->>'from') IS NOT NULL
      AND (pw.wage_details->'prevailing_wage'->>'value') IS NOT NULL
      AND (pw.wage_details->'offered_wage'->>'unit')
          = (pw.wage_details->'prevailing_wage'->>'unit')
),
case_differences AS (
    SELECT
        filekey,
        job_title,
        (offered_pay - prevailing_pay) * 100.0 / prevailing_pay
            AS pay_difference_pct
    FROM comparable_cases
    WHERE offered_pay IS NOT NULL
      AND prevailing_pay IS NOT NULL
      AND prevailing_pay > 0
),
qualifying_jobs AS (
    SELECT
        job_title,
        COUNT(DISTINCT filekey) AS application_count,
        AVG(pay_difference_pct) AS avg_pay_difference_pct

    GROUP BY job_title
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT filekey) >= 30

)
SELECT

    application_count AS applications,
    ROUND(avg_pay_difference_pct, 2) AS average_percentage_pay_difference,

FROM qualifying_jobs

LIMIT 5;
```

I classified attorneys with **more than 80%** of their cases in one visa type as Specialists. Those handling 2–3 visa types without exceeding that threshold are Hybrid Practitioners; the remaining attorneys are Generalists. The strict “more than 80%” threshold puts the attorney at exactly 80% in the Hybrid Practitioner group.

```sql
WITH attorney_visa_counts AS (
    SELECT
        ca.counselmail,
        c.visacls::VARCHAR AS visa_type,
        COUNT(*) AS case_count
    FROM case_attorney AS ca
    JOIN cases AS c
        ON c.filekey = ca.docketkey
    GROUP BY ca.counselmail, c.visacls
),
attorney_stats AS (
    SELECT
        counselmail,
        SUM(case_count) AS total_cases,
        COUNT(*) AS visa_type_count,
        MAX(case_count)::DOUBLE / SUM(case_count) AS main_type_share
    FROM attorney_visa_counts
    GROUP BY counselmail
    HAVING SUM(case_count) >= 5
),
categorized AS (
    SELECT
        *,
        CASE
            WHEN main_type_share > 0.80 THEN 'Specialist'
            WHEN visa_type_count BETWEEN 2 AND 3 THEN 'Hybrid Practitioner'
            ELSE 'Generalist'
        END AS category_name,
        1.0 - visa_type_count / 4.0 AS specialization_score
    FROM attorney_stats
)
SELECT
    category_name,
    COUNT(*) AS attorney_count,
    ROUND(AVG(specialization_score), 2) AS avg_specialization_score,
    ROUND(AVG(main_type_share) * 100, 2) AS avg_main_visa_type_case_pct
FROM categorized
GROUP BY category_name
ORDER BY attorney_count DESC, category_name;
```

I treated the wage difference as **offered wage minus prevailing wage**. For offered wage ranges, I used the midpoint when an upper value was provided; otherwise, I used the lower value. I required offered and prevailing units to match for each record, and included only industries with one consistent unit across their qualifying applications.

| NAICS code | Job applications | Average wage difference |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 621512 | 1 | 450,999.00 |
| 621498 | 1 | 211,789.00 |
| 541110 | 2 | 154,880.00 |
| 523940 | 1 | 105,549.00 |
| 31199 | 1 | 100,710.00 |

```sql
WITH wage_rows AS (
  SELECT
    c.filekey,
    e.employer_contact_info->>'naics_code' AS naics_code,
    pw.wage_details->'offered_wage'->>'unit' AS offered_unit,
    pw.wage_details->'prevailing_wage'->>'unit' AS prevailing_unit,
    TRY_CAST(
      REGEXP_REPLACE(
        pw.wage_details->'offered_wage'->>'from',
        '[^0-9.-]', '', 'g'
      ) AS DOUBLE
    ) AS offered_from,
    TRY_CAST(
      REGEXP_REPLACE(
        pw.wage_details->'offered_wage'->>'to',
        '[^0-9.-]', '', 'g'
      ) AS DOUBLE
    ) AS offered_to,
    TRY_CAST(
      REGEXP_REPLACE(
        pw.wage_details->'prevailing_wage'->>'value',
        '[^0-9.-]', '', 'g'
      ) AS DOUBLE
    ) AS prevailing_wage
  FROM cases c
  JOIN employer e
    ON c.homefirm = e.corphandle
   AND c.homezip = e.zipref
  JOIN case_worksite cw
    ON c.filekey = cw.dockkey
  JOIN prevailing_wage pw
    ON cw.wagetrack = pw.trackno
),
eligible AS (
  SELECT
    filekey,
    naics_code,
    offered_unit,
    CASE
      WHEN offered_to > offered_from
        THEN (offered_from + offered_to) / 2.0
      ELSE offered_from
    END - prevailing_wage AS wage_difference
  FROM wage_rows
  WHERE REGEXP_MATCHES(naics_code, '^[0-9]{2,6}$')
    AND offered_unit = prevailing_unit
    AND offered_from IS NOT NULL
    AND prevailing_wage IS NOT NULL
),
industry AS (
  SELECT
    naics_code,
    COUNT(DISTINCT offered_unit) AS unit_count,
    COUNT(DISTINCT filekey) AS job_applications,
    AVG(wage_difference) AS avg_difference
  FROM eligible
  GROUP BY naics_code
)
SELECT
  naics_code,
  job_applications,
  ROUND(avg_difference, 2) AS avg_wage_difference
FROM industry
WHERE unit_count = 1
ORDER BY avg_difference DESC, job_applications DESC, naics_code
LIMIT 5;
```

Using the standardized occupation title (`socTitle`), I averaged the wage differential across applications with both pay figures present and matching pay units. Three occupations meet the 30-application threshold and have an average differential above 10%.

| Job title | Applications | Average pay difference | Classification |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Computer and Information Systems Managers | 38 | 19.89% | Skill Shortage Occupation |

```sql
WITH parsed AS (
  SELECT
    c.filekey,
    c.soctitle,
    pw.wage_details->'offered_wage'->>'unit' AS offered_unit,
    pw.wage_details->'prevailing_wage'->>'unit' AS prevailing_unit,
    TRY_CAST(
      REPLACE(REPLACE(pw.wage_details->'offered_wage'->>'from', '$', ''), ',', '')
      AS DOUBLE
    ) AS offered_wage,
    TRY_CAST(
      REPLACE(REPLACE(pw.wage_details->'prevailing_wage'->>'value', 'USD', ''), ',', '')
      AS DOUBLE
    ) AS prevailing_wage
  FROM main.cases AS c
  JOIN main.case_worksite AS cw
    ON cw.dockkey = c.filekey
  JOIN main.prevailing_wage AS pw
    ON pw.trackno = cw.wagetrack
),
differentials AS (
  SELECT
    filekey,
    soctitle,
    100.0 * (
      offered_wage * CASE offered_unit
        WHEN 'Hour' THEN 2080
        WHEN 'Week' THEN 52
        WHEN 'Month' THEN 12
        WHEN 'Year' THEN 1
      END
      -
      prevailing_wage * CASE prevailing_unit
        WHEN 'Hour' THEN 2080
        WHEN 'Week' THEN 52
        WHEN 'Month' THEN 12
        WHEN 'Year' THEN 1
      END
    ) / (
      prevailing_wage * CASE prevailing_unit
        WHEN 'Hour' THEN 2080
        WHEN 'Week' THEN 52
        WHEN 'Month' THEN 12
        WHEN 'Year' THEN 1
      END
    ) AS pay_difference_pct
  FROM parsed
  WHERE offered_unit IS NOT NULL
    AND offered_unit = prevailing_unit
    AND offered_wage IS NOT NULL
    AND prevailing_wage IS NOT NULL
    AND prevailing_wage > 0
)
SELECT
  soctitle AS job_title,
  COUNT(DISTINCT filekey) AS application_count,
  ROUND(AVG(pay_difference_pct), 2) AS average_pay_difference_pct,
  'Skill Shortage Occupation' AS classification
FROM differentials
GROUP BY soctitle
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT filekey) >= 30
  AND AVG(pay_difference_pct) > 10
ORDER BY average_pay_difference_pct DESC
LIMIT 5;
```

Using the documented thresholds, I classified attorneys with **more than 80%** of cases in one visa type as Specialists, those with a largest share of **50% or less** as Generalists, and the remaining mix as Hybrid Practitioners. The specialization score is `1 − distinct visa types handled / distinct visa types overall`. Among attorneys with at least five cases, the results are:

| Category | Attorneys | Avg. specialization score | Avg. cases in main visa type |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Specialist | 20 | 0.70 | 98.59% |
| Hybrid Practitioner | 1 | 0.50 | 80.00% |

```sql
WITH per_type AS (
    SELECT
        ca.counselmail,
        c.visacls,
        COUNT(*) AS type_cases
    FROM case_attorney AS ca
    JOIN cases AS c
        ON c.filekey = ca.docketkey
    GROUP BY ca.counselmail, c.visacls
),
attorney_mix AS (
    SELECT
        counselmail,
        SUM(type_cases) AS total_cases,
        COUNT(*) AS distinct_visa_types,
        MAX(type_cases) AS main_type_cases
    FROM per_type
    GROUP BY counselmail
    HAVING SUM(type_cases) >= 5
),
scored AS (
    SELECT
        counselmail,
        1.0 - distinct_visa_types::DOUBLE
            / (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT visacls) FROM cases) AS specialization_score,
        100.0 * main_type_cases / total_cases AS main_type_pct,
        main_type_cases::DOUBLE / total_cases AS main_type_share
    FROM attorney_mix
),
categorized AS (
    SELECT
        *,
        CASE
            WHEN main_type_share > 0.80 THEN 'Specialist'
            WHEN main_type_share <= 0.50 THEN 'Generalist'
            ELSE 'Hybrid Practitioner'
        END AS category_name
    FROM scored
)
SELECT
    category_name,
    COUNT(*) AS attorney_count,
    ROUND(AVG(specialization_score), 2) AS avg_specialization_score,
    ROUND(AVG(main_type_pct), 2) AS avg_main_visa_type_case_percentage
FROM categorized
GROUP BY category_name
ORDER BY attorney_count DESC, category_name;
```

```sql
WITH latest_assessment AS (
    SELECT
        e.pat_ref AS patient_id,
        e.ab_ref AS assessment_id,
        e.enc_key,
        e.time_mark,
        f.env_stress AS facility_stress,
        s.suic_risk
    FROM encounters e
    JOIN facilities f
        ON f.fac_key = e.fac_id
    JOIN assessmentsymptomsandrisk s
        ON s.asr_key = e.ab_ref
    WHERE e.ab_ref IS NOT NULL
    QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
        PARTITION BY e.pat_ref
        ORDER BY e.time_mark DESC, e.enc_key DESC
    ) = 1
),
engagement AS (
    SELECT
        la.patient_id,
        la.assessment_id,
        la.time_mark,
        CAST(la.time_mark AS DATE) AS latest_assessment_date,
        la.facility_stress,
        AVG(
            CASE lower(t.th_eng)
                WHEN 'non-compliant' THEN 1.0
                WHEN 'low' THEN 2.0
                WHEN 'medium' THEN 3.0
                WHEN 'high' THEN 4.0
            END
        ) AS avg_engagement_score
    FROM latest_assessment la
    JOIN treatmentbasics t
        ON t.enc_ref = la.enc_key
    WHERE la.facility_stress = 'Severe'
      AND la.suic_risk IN ('High', 'Severe')
    GROUP BY
        la.patient_id,
        la.assessment_id,
        la.time_mark,
        CAST(la.time_mark AS DATE),
        la.facility_stress
    HAVING AVG(
        CASE lower(t.th_eng)
            WHEN 'non-compliant' THEN 1.0
            WHEN 'low' THEN 2.0
            WHEN 'medium' THEN 3.0
            WHEN 'high' THEN 4.0
        END
    ) <= 2
)
SELECT
    patient_id,
    assessment_id,
    latest_assessment_date,
    ROUND(avg_engagement_score) AS avg_engagement_score,
    facility_stress
FROM engagement
ORDER BY time_mark DESC, assessment_id
LIMIT 50;
```

    JOIN facilities f
        ON f.fac_key = e.fac_id
    JOIN assessmentsymptomsandrisk s
        ON s.asr_key = e.ab_ref
    WHERE e.ab_ref IS NOT NULL
    QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
        PARTITION BY e.pat_ref
        ORDER BY e.time_mark DESC, e.enc_key DESC
    ) = 1
),
engagement AS (
    SELECT
        la.patient_id,
        la.assessment_id,
        la.time_mark,
        CAST(la.time_mark AS DATE) AS latest_assessment_date,
        la.facility_stress,
        AVG(
            CASE lower(t.th_eng)
                WHEN 'non-compliant' THEN 1.0
                WHEN 'low' THEN 2.0
                WHEN 'medium' THEN 3.0
                WHEN 'high' THEN 4.0
            END
        ) AS avg_engagement_score
    FROM latest_assessment la
    JOIN treatmentbasics t
        ON t.enc_ref = la.enc_key
    WHERE la.facility_stress = 'Severe'
      AND la.suic_risk IN ('High', 'Severe')
    GROUP BY
        la.patient_id,
        la.assessment_id,
        la.time_mark,
        CAST(la.time_mark AS DATE),
        la.facility_stress
    HAVING AVG(
        CASE lower(t.th_eng)
            WHEN 'non-compliant' THEN 1.0
            WHEN 'low' THEN 2.0
            WHEN 'medium' THEN 3.0
            WHEN 'high' THEN 4.0
        END
    ) <= 2
)
SELECT
    patient_id,
    assessment_id,
    latest_assessment_date,
    ROUND(avg_engagement_score) AS avg_engagement_score,
    facility_stress
FROM engagement
ORDER BY time_mark DESC, assessment_id
LIMIT 50;

Using the wage differential rate, **((offered wage − prevailing wage) / prevailing wage) × 100**, the top five industries are:

|---|---:|---:|

The query includes six-digit NAICS codes and wage records whose offered and prevailing wage units match. It averages worksite wage differences within each application before calculating the industry average.

```sql
WITH wage_obs AS (
  SELECT
    c.filekey,
    json_extract_string(e.employer_contact_info, '$.naics_code') AS naics_code,
    TRY_CAST(
      regexp_replace(
        json_extract_string(p.wage_details, '$.offered_wage.from'),
        '[^0-9.]', '', 'g'
      ) AS DOUBLE
    ) AS offered,
    TRY_CAST(
      regexp_replace(
        json_extract_string(p.wage_details, '$.prevailing_wage.value'),
        '[^0-9.]', '', 'g'
      ) AS DOUBLE
    ) AS prevailing
  FROM cases c
  JOIN employer e
    ON e.corphandle = c.homefirm
   AND e.zipref = c.homezip
  JOIN case_worksite cw
    ON cw.dockkey = c.filekey
  JOIN prevailing_wage p
    ON p.trackno = cw.wagetrack
  WHERE regexp_matches(
          json_extract_string(e.employer_contact_info, '$.naics_code'),
          '^[0-9]{6}$'
        )
    AND json_extract_string(p.wage_details, '$.offered_wage.unit')
        = json_extract_string(p.wage_details, '$.prevailing_wage.unit')
),
per_application AS (
  SELECT
    naics_code,
    filekey,
    AVG((offered - prevailing) / prevailing * 100) AS app_wdr
  FROM wage_obs
  WHERE offered IS NOT NULL
    AND prevailing > 0
  GROUP BY naics_code, filekey
),
industry AS (
  SELECT
    naics_code,
    COUNT(*) AS application_count,
    AVG(app_wdr) AS avg_wdr
  FROM per_application
  GROUP BY naics_code
)
SELECT
  naics_code,
  application_count,
  ROUND(avg_wdr, 2) AS avg_industry_wage_difference_pct
FROM industry
ORDER BY avg_wdr DESC
LIMIT 5;
```

Using the specialization definition, attorneys with more than 80% of their cases in one visa type are Specialists; those handling 2–3 visa types without that concentration are Hybrid Practitioners; the remaining attorneys are Generalists. Only Specialists and Hybrid Practitioners meet the five-case threshold in this data.

| Category | Attorneys | Avg. specialization score | Avg. cases in main visa type (%) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Specialists | 20 | 0.70 | 98.59 |
| Hybrid Practitioners | 1 | 0.50 | 80.00 |

```sql
WITH visa_types AS (
    SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT visacls) AS total_visa_types
    FROM main.cases
),
attorney_visa_counts AS (
    SELECT
        ca.counselmail,
        c.visacls,
        COUNT(*) AS cases_in_visa_type
    FROM main.case_attorney ca
    JOIN main.cases c
        ON c.filekey = ca.docketkey
    GROUP BY ca.counselmail, c.visacls
),
attorney_stats AS (
    SELECT
        counselmail,
        SUM(cases_in_visa_type) AS total_cases,
        COUNT(DISTINCT visacls) AS visa_types_handled,
        MAX(cases_in_visa_type) AS main_visa_type_cases
    FROM attorney_visa_counts
    GROUP BY counselmail
),
attorney_classification AS (
    SELECT
        s.counselmail,
        s.total_cases,
        1.0 - (s.visa_types_handled::DOUBLE / vt.total_visa_types)
            AS specialization_score,
        100.0 * s.main_visa_type_cases / s.total_cases
            AS main_visa_type_case_percentage,
        CASE
            WHEN 1.0 * s.main_visa_type_cases / s.total_cases > 0.80
                THEN 'Specialists'
            WHEN s.visa_types_handled BETWEEN 2 AND 3
                THEN 'Hybrid Practitioners'
            ELSE 'Generalists'
        END AS category_name
    FROM attorney_stats s
    CROSS JOIN visa_types vt
    WHERE s.total_cases >= 5
)
SELECT
    category_name,
    COUNT(*) AS attorney_count,
    ROUND(AVG(specialization_score), 2) AS avg_specialization_score,
    ROUND(AVG(main_visa_type_case_percentage), 2)
        AS avg_main_visa_type_case_percentage
FROM attorney_classification
GROUP BY category_name
ORDER BY attorney_count DESC, category_name;
```

answer:
Using a 0–100 score, I scored support-service breadth as the share of four listed services available (Case Management, Employment, Housing, Legal), and community resources as Limited = 0, Adequate = 50, Comprehensive = 100. A facility’s resource score is the average of the components that are recorded. I defined adherence rate as the share of recorded treatment-outcome adherence values that are High or Compliant; facilities without a rate are excluded from the correlation.

The average resource score is **47.14/100** across **476** facilities with at least one resource measure recorded. The Pearson correlation with adherence rate is **0.137** across **162** facilities with both measures—a weak positive association.

```sql
WITH service_counts AS (
    SELECT
        f.fac_key,
        COUNT(DISTINCT trim(tok)) FILTER (
            WHERE trim(tok) IN ('Case Management', 'Employment', 'Housing', 'Legal')
        ) AS service_count
    FROM facilities f,
         UNNEST(string_split(f.spt_svc, ',')) AS u(tok)
    WHERE f.spt_svc IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY f.fac_key
),
facility_scores AS (
    SELECT
        f.fac_key,
        CASE
            WHEN sc.fac_key IS NOT NULL THEN 100.0 * sc.service_count / 4.0
        END AS service_score,
        CASE lower(trim(f.com_res))
            WHEN 'limited' THEN 0.0
            WHEN 'adequate' THEN 50.0
            WHEN 'comprehensive' THEN 100.0
        END AS community_score
    FROM facilities f
    LEFT JOIN service_counts sc ON sc.fac_key = f.fac_key
),
resource_scores AS (
    SELECT
        fac_key,
        (COALESCE(service_score, 0.0) + COALESCE(community_score, 0.0)) /
        (
            CASE WHEN service_score IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END +
            CASE WHEN community_score IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
        ) AS resource_score
    FROM facility_scores
    WHERE service_score IS NOT NULL OR community_score IS NOT NULL
),
facility_adherence AS (
    SELECT
        e.fac_id AS fac_key,
        COUNT(*) FILTER (
            WHERE lower(trim(o.txprogmet ->> 'Tx_Adh')) IN ('high', 'compliant')
        ) * 1.0 /
        NULLIF(
            COUNT(*) FILTER (
                WHERE lower(trim(o.txprogmet ->> 'Tx_Adh'))
                    IN ('high', 'medium', 'low', 'compliant', 'non-compliant')
            ),
            0
        ) AS adherence_rate
    FROM treatmentoutcomes o
    JOIN treatmentbasics tb ON tb.tx_key = o.tx_ref
    JOIN encounters e ON e.enc_key = tb.enc_ref
    GROUP BY e.fac_id
)
SELECT
    AVG(rs.resource_score) AS overall_resource_score,
    corr(rs.resource_score, fa.adherence_rate) AS resource_adherence_correlation,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE fa.adherence_rate IS NOT NULL) AS facilities_in_correlation
FROM resource_scores rs
LEFT JOIN facility_adherence fa ON fa.fac_key = rs.fac_key;
```

Treatment adherence is the percentage of outcome records rated **High** or **Compliant**; patient stability is the percentage of linked assessment records with recovery status **Stable**. Facilities are ranked by the average of those two rates, and quadrant cutoffs are the mean rates across eligible facilities. Facilities without data for either measure are excluded.

```sql
WITH adherence AS (
    SELECT
        e.fac_id,
        100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (
            WHERE lower(json_extract_string(o.txprogmet, '$.Tx_Adh'))
                  IN ('high', 'compliant')
        ) / NULLIF(
            COUNT(*) FILTER (
                WHERE json_extract_string(o.txprogmet, '$.Tx_Adh') IS NOT NULL
            ),
            0
        ) AS adherence_rate
    FROM encounters e
    JOIN treatmentbasics t ON t.enc_ref = e.enc_key
    JOIN treatmentoutcomes o ON o.tx_ref = t.tx_key
    WHERE e.fac_id IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY e.fac_id
),
stability AS (
    SELECT
        e.fac_id,
        100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (
            WHERE lower(s.rec_status) = 'stable'
        ) / NULLIF(
            COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE s.rec_status IS NOT NULL),
            0
        ) AS stability_rate
    FROM encounters e
```

answer:
I treated **Patient Stability Metric (PSM)** as the clinician’s average housing-stability score among their assigned patients: Stable = 4, At Risk = 3, Unstable = 2, and Homeless = 1. I treated a facility as resource-backed when it has documented support services (excluding entries containing “None”) and Adequate or Comprehensive community resources.

```sql
WITH clinician_stability AS (
  SELECT
    c.clin_key AS clinician_id,
    f.fac_key AS facility_id,
    AVG(
      CASE lower(p.house_stable)
        WHEN 'stable' THEN 4.0
        WHEN 'at risk' THEN 3.0
        WHEN 'unstable' THEN 2.0
        WHEN 'homeless' THEN 1.0
      END
    ) AS patient_stability_metric
  FROM clinicians c
  JOIN facilities f
    ON f.fac_key = c.fac_connect
  JOIN patients p
    ON p.clin_lead_ref = c.clin_key
  WHERE lower(f.com_res) IN ('adequate', 'comprehensive')
    AND f.spt_svc IS NOT NULL
    AND trim(f.spt_svc) <> ''
    AND lower(f.spt_svc) NOT LIKE '%none%'
  GROUP BY c.clin_key, f.fac_key
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT
    clinician_id,
    facility_id,
    patient_stability_metric,
    RANK() OVER (
      PARTITION BY facility_id
      ORDER BY patient_stability_metric DESC
    ) AS facility_rank
  FROM clinician_stability
)
SELECT
  clinician_id,
  facility_id,
  patient_stability_metric,
  facility_rank
FROM ranked
ORDER BY facility_id, facility_rank, clinician_id
LIMIT 100;
```

I scored therapy engagement as Non-compliant = 0, Low = 1, Medium = 2, and High = 3. The recovery trajectory index is the average of treatment-goal and recovery-goal status scores, each mapped from Not Started = 0 through Achieved = 3, with Modified = 2. I treated engagement averages of at least 2.5 as high and recovery indices below 1.5 as lagging.

```sql
WITH facility_metrics AS (
    SELECT
        f.fac_key AS facility_id,
        AVG(
            CASE LOWER(t.th_eng)
                WHEN 'non-compliant' THEN 0.0
                WHEN 'low' THEN 1.0
                WHEN 'medium' THEN 2.0
                WHEN 'high' THEN 3.0
            END
        ) AS avg_engagement,
        AVG((
            CASE o.tx_goal_stat
                WHEN 'Not Started' THEN 0.0
                WHEN 'In Progress' THEN 1.0
                WHEN 'Modified' THEN 2.0
                WHEN 'Achieved' THEN 3.0
            END
            +
            CASE o.rec_goal_stat
                WHEN 'Not Started' THEN 0.0
                WHEN 'In Progress' THEN 1.0
                WHEN 'Modified' THEN 2.0
                WHEN 'Achieved' THEN 3.0
            END
        ) / 2.0) AS recovery_index
    FROM treatmentbasics t
    JOIN encounters e ON e.enc_key = t.enc_ref
    JOIN facilities f ON f.fac_key = e.fac_id
    JOIN treatmentoutcomes o ON o.tx_ref = t.tx_key
    WHERE t.th_eng IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY f.fac_key
)
SELECT
    facility_id,
    ROUND(avg_engagement, 2) AS avg_therapy_engagement_score,
    ROUND(recovery_index, 2) AS recovery_trajectory_index
FROM facility_metrics
WHERE avg_engagement >= 2.5
  AND recovery_index < 1.5
ORDER BY facility_id
LIMIT 100;
```

Using the latest assessment for each patient, I treated **high-risk** as High suicide risk or PHQ-9 > 15 or GAD-7 > 15. I interpreted **severe facility stress** as `env_stress = 'Severe'` and **poor therapy engagement** as an average engagement score below 1.5 with the latest therapy record rated Low.

```sql
WITH ranked_assessments AS (
    SELECT
        e.pat_ref AS patient_id,
        e.ab_ref AS assessment_id,
        e.time_mark AS assessment_time,
        CAST(e.time_mark AS DATE) AS assessment_date,

        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
```

The average resource adequacy score across facilities with a recorded community-resource rating is **2.02** (on the 1–3 scale). The correlation with treatment adherence rate is **0.325**, indicating a modest positive relationship. Facilities without a treatment adherence rate are excluded from the correlation.

```sql
WITH facility_resources AS (
    SELECT
        fac_key,
        CASE
            WHEN LOWER(TRIM(com_res)) IN ('comprehensive', 'extensive') THEN 3.0
            WHEN LOWER(TRIM(com_res)) = 'adequate' THEN 2.0
            WHEN LOWER(TRIM(com_res)) = 'limited' THEN 1.0
        END AS resource_adequacy_score
    FROM facilities
),
facility_adherence AS (
    SELECT
        e.fac_id AS fac_key,
        COUNT(*) FILTER (
            WHERE LOWER(JSON_EXTRACT_STRING(o.txprogmet, '$.Tx_Adh'))
                IN ('high', 'medium', 'compliant')
        )::DOUBLE / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) AS treatment_adherence_rate
    FROM treatmentoutcomes o
    JOIN treatmentbasics t ON t.tx_key = o.tx_ref
    JOIN encounters e ON e.enc_key = t.enc_ref
    GROUP BY e.fac_id
),
all_facility_scores AS (
    SELECT AVG(resource_adequacy_score) AS overall_avg_resource_adequacy_score
    FROM facility_resources
),
correlation AS (
    SELECT CORR(r.resource_adequacy_score, a.treatment_adherence_rate)
           AS resource_adherence_correlation
    FROM facility_resources r
    JOIN facility_adherence a ON a.fac_key = r.fac_key
    WHERE a.treatment_adherence_rate IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT *
```

I calculated each clinician’s PSM from their assigned patients: total crisis interventions and missed appointments per patient, combined using the defined PSM formula. Clinicians are ranked within their facility, with ties receiving the same rank. Only clinicians in facilities rated Adequate, Comprehensive, or Extensive for community resources are included.

```sql
WITH missed_by_patient AS (
    SELECT
        pat_ref,
        SUM(COALESCE(miss_appt, 0)) AS missed_total
    FROM encounters
    WHERE pat_ref IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY pat_ref
),
crisis_by_patient AS (
    SELECT
        e.pat_ref,
        SUM(COALESCE(t.crisis_int, 0)) AS crisis_total
    FROM encounters e
    JOIN treatmentbasics t
        ON t.enc_ref = e.enc_key
    WHERE e.pat_ref IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY e.pat_ref
),
clinician_scores AS (
    SELECT
        c.clin_key AS clinician_id,
        f.fac_key AS facility_id,
        1.0 / (
            1.0
            + SUM(COALESCE(cr.crisis_total, 0)) / COUNT(*)
            + SUM(COALESCE(mp.missed_total, 0)) / COUNT(*)
        ) AS patient_stability_metric
    FROM clinicians c
    JOIN facilities f
        ON f.fac_key = c.fac_connect
    JOIN patients p
        ON p.clin_lead_ref = c.clin_key
    LEFT JOIN missed_by_patient mp
        ON mp.pat_ref = p.pat_key
    LEFT JOIN crisis_by_patient cr
        ON cr.pat_ref = p.pat_key
    WHERE f.com_res IN ('Adequate', 'Comprehensive', 'Extensive')
    GROUP BY c.clin_key, f.fac_key
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT
        clinician_id,
        facility_id,
        patient_stability_metric,
        RANK() OVER (
            PARTITION BY facility_id
            ORDER BY patient_stability_metric DESC
        ) AS facility_rank
    FROM clinician_scores
)
SELECT
    clinician_id,
    facility_id,
    patient_stability_metric,
    facility_rank
FROM ranked
ORDER BY facility_id, facility_rank, clinician_id
LIMIT 100;
```

The query returns 100 facilities with both metrics available, sorted by performance quadrant and then facility ID. Quadrants use the median adherence rate (0.50) and median stability score (about 0.17) across facilities with available metrics.

```sql
WITH encounter_rollup AS (
    SELECT fac_id,
           COUNT(DISTINCT pat_ref) AS patient_count,
           SUM(COALESCE(miss_appt, 0)) AS missed_appts
    FROM encounters
    GROUP BY fac_id
),
crisis_rollup AS (
    SELECT e.fac_id,
           SUM(COALESCE(tb.crisis_int, 0)) AS crisis_interventions
    FROM treatmentbasics AS tb
    JOIN encounters AS e ON e.enc_key = tb.enc_ref
    GROUP BY e.fac_id
),
outcome_rollup AS (
    SELECT e.fac_id,
           COUNT(*) AS outcome_count,
           SUM(
               CASE
                   WHEN lower(trim(json_extract_string(txo.txprogmet, '$.Tx_Adh')))
                        IN ('high', 'medium', 'compliant')
                   THEN 1
                   ELSE 0
               END
           ) AS adherent_count
    FROM treatmentoutcomes AS txo
    JOIN treatmentbasics AS tb ON tb.tx_key = txo.tx_ref
    JOIN encounters AS e ON e.enc_key = tb.enc_ref
    GROUP BY e.fac_id
),
facility_metrics AS (
    SELECT f.fac_key,
           1.0 * o.adherent_count / NULLIF(o.outcome_count, 0) AS adherence_rate,
           1.0 / (
               1 + (
                   COALESCE(c.crisis_interventions, 0)
                   + COALESCE(er.missed_appts, 0)
               ) / NULLIF(er.patient_count, 0)
           ) AS stability
    FROM facilities AS f
    LEFT JOIN encounter_rollup AS er ON er.fac_id = f.fac_key
    LEFT JOIN crisis_rollup AS c ON c.fac_id = f.fac_key
    LEFT JOIN outcome_rollup AS o ON o.fac_id = f.fac_key
),
thresholds AS (
    SELECT median(adherence_rate) AS median_adherence,
           median(stability) AS median_stability
    FROM facility_metrics
),
classified AS (
    SELECT fm.fac_key,
           fm.adherence_rate,
           fm.stability,
           CASE
               WHEN fm.adherence_rate >= t.median_adherence
                    AND fm.stability >= t.median_stability
                   THEN 'High Adherence / High Stability'
               WHEN fm.adherence_rate >= t.median_adherence
                    AND fm.stability < t.median_stability
                   THEN 'High Adherence / Low Stability'
               WHEN fm.adherence_rate < t.median_adherence
                    AND fm.stability >= t.median_stability
                   THEN 'Low Adherence / High Stability'
               ELSE 'Low Adherence / Low Stability'
           END AS performance_quadrant
    FROM facility_metrics AS fm
    CROSS JOIN thresholds AS t
    WHERE fm.adherence_rate IS NOT NULL
      AND fm.stability IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT fac_key AS facility_id,
       ROUND(adherence_rate, 2) AS treatment_adherence_rate,
       ROUND(stability, 2) AS patient_stability,
       performance_quadrant
FROM classified
ORDER BY performance_quadrant, facility_id
LIMIT 100;
```

Using **six-digit numeric NAICS codes** and including only applications whose offered-wage and prevailing-wage units match, the top industries by average wage difference are:

| NAICS code | Applications | Average wage difference |
|---|---:|---:|
| 621498 | 1 | 360.94% |
| 621111 | 5 | 121.13% |
| 523940 | 1 | 115.98% |
| 621512 | 1 | 113.96% |
| 541110 | 2 | 106.92% |

The wage difference is the average percentage difference between offered and prevailing wages.

```sql
WITH eligible AS (
    SELECT
        c.filekey,
        e.employer_contact_info->>'naics_code' AS naics_code,
        CAST(REPLACE(REPLACE(pw.wage_details->'offered_wage'->>'from', '$', ''), ',', '') AS DOUBLE) AS offered_wage,
        CAST(REPLACE(REPLACE(pw.wage_details->'prevailing_wage'->>'value', 'USD', ''), ',', '') AS DOUBLE) AS prevailing_wage,
        pw.wage_details->'offered_wage'->>'unit' AS offered_unit,
        pw.wage_details->'prevailing_wage'->>'unit' AS prevailing_unit
    FROM cases c
    JOIN employer e
      ON c.homefirm = e.corphandle
     AND c.homezip = e.zipref
    JOIN case_worksite cw
      ON cw.dockkey = c.filekey
    JOIN prevailing_wage pw
      ON pw.trackno = cw.wagetrack
    WHERE regexp_full_match(
              COALESCE(e.employer_contact_info->>'naics_code', ''),
              '[0-9]{6}'
          )
      AND (pw.wage_details->'offered_wage'->>'unit')
          = (pw.wage_details->'prevailing_wage'->>'unit')
      AND (pw.wage_details->'offered_wage'->>'unit')
          IN ('Hour', 'Week', 'Month', 'Year')
)
SELECT
    naics_code,
    COUNT(DISTINCT filekey) AS application_count,
    ROUND(AVG(((offered_wage - prevailing_wage) / prevailing_wage) * 100), 2)
        AS avg_industry_wage_difference
FROM eligible
GROUP BY naics_code
ORDER BY avg_industry_wage_difference DESC
LIMIT 5;
```

answer:
I computed a PSM for each clinician’s encounters at their linked facility, applying the stability formula to that clinician’s caseload. Facilities are included when their community resources are Adequate, Comprehensive, or Extensive. Clinicians are ranked within each facility, with ties sharing a rank.

```sql
WITH clinician_encounters AS (
    SELECT
        c.clin_key,
        c.fac_connect AS fac_key,
        COUNT(DISTINCT e.pat_ref) AS patient_count,
        COALESCE(SUM(e.miss_appt), 0) AS missed_appts
    FROM clinicians c
    JOIN facilities f
      ON f.fac_key = c.fac_connect
    JOIN encounters e
      ON e.clin_id = c.clin_key
     AND e.fac_id = c.fac_connect
    WHERE f.com_res IN ('Adequate', 'Comprehensive', 'Extensive')
    GROUP BY c.clin_key, c.fac_connect
),
clinician_crisis AS (
    SELECT
        c.clin_key,
        c.fac_connect AS fac_key,
        COALESCE(SUM(tb.crisis_int), 0) AS crisis_interventions
    FROM clinicians c
    JOIN facilities f
      ON f.fac_key = c.fac_connect
    JOIN encounters e
      ON e.clin_id = c.clin_key
     AND e.fac_id = c.fac_connect
    LEFT JOIN treatmentbasics tb
      ON tb.enc_ref = e.enc_key
    WHERE f.com_res IN ('Adequate', 'Comprehensive', 'Extensive')
    GROUP BY c.clin_key, c.fac_connect
),
clinician_psm AS (
    SELECT
        ce.clin_key,
        ce.fac_key,
        1.0 / (
            1
            + cc.crisis_interventions / ce.patient_count
            + ce.missed_appts / ce.patient_count
        ) AS patient_stability_metric
    FROM clinician_encounters ce
    JOIN clinician_crisis cc
      ON cc.clin_key = ce.clin_key
     AND cc.fac_key = ce.fac_key
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT
        clin_key,
        fac_key,
        patient_stability_metric,
        RANK() OVER (
            PARTITION BY fac_key
            ORDER BY patient_stability_metric DESC
        ) AS facility_rank
    FROM clinician_psm
)
SELECT
    clin_key AS clinician_id,
    fac_key AS facility_id,
    patient_stability_metric,
    facility_rank
FROM ranked
ORDER BY facility_id, facility_rank, clinician_id
LIMIT 100;
```

The criteria return **4 patients**. I used the governed high-risk definition (high suicide risk or PHQ-9 > 15 or GAD-7 > 15) and low-engagement definition (average engagement below 1.5, with at least one Low-engagement treatment record). The assessment and facility are taken from each patient’s latest encounter linked to an assessment.

| Patient ID | Assessment ID | Latest assessment date | Avg. engagement score | Facility stress |

| P277881 | A758003 | 2025-02-19 | 1.00 | Severe |
| P338303 | A787205 | 2025-02-19 | 1.00 | Severe |

```sql
WITH patient_engagement AS (
    SELECT
        e.pat_ref AS patient_id,
        AVG(CASE t.th_eng WHEN 'High' THEN 3 WHEN 'Medium' THEN 2 WHEN 'Low' THEN 1 END) AS avg_engagement_score,
        BOOL_OR(t.th_eng = 'Low') AS has_low_engagement
    FROM main.treatmentbasics AS t
    JOIN main.encounters AS e ON e.enc_key = t.enc_ref
    GROUP BY e.pat_ref
), latest_assessment AS (
    SELECT
        a.pat_owner_ref AS patient_id,
        a.ab_key AS assessment_id,
        CAST(e.time_mark AS DATE) AS assessment_date,
        e.fac_id AS facility_id,
        s.suic_risk,
        s.phq9_scr,
        s.gad7_scr,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY a.pat_owner_ref
            ORDER BY e.time_mark DESC, a.ab_key DESC
        ) AS rn
    FROM main.assessmentbasics AS a
    JOIN main.encounters AS e
      ON e.ab_ref = a.ab_key AND e.pat_ref = a.pat_owner_ref
    LEFT JOIN main.assessmentsymptomsandrisk AS s ON s.asr_key = a.ab_key
)
SELECT
    la.patient_id,
    la.assessment_id,
    la.assessment_date AS latest_assessment_date,
    ROUND(pe.avg_engagement_score, 2) AS avg_engagement_score,
    f.env_stress AS facility_stress_level
FROM latest_assessment AS la
JOIN patient_engagement AS pe ON pe.patient_id = la.patient_id
JOIN main.facilities AS f ON f.fac_key = la.facility_id
WHERE la.rn = 1
  AND (la.suic_risk = 'High' OR la.phq9_scr > 15 OR la.gad7_scr > 15)
  AND f.env_stress = 'Severe'
  AND pe.avg_engagement_score < 1.5

ORDER BY la.assessment_date DESC, la.patient_id
LIMIT 50;
```

Across facilities with recorded community-resource ratings, the **average resource adequacy score is 2.02** (on the defined 1–3 scale). The correlation between facility resource score and treatment adherence rate is **0.325**, a positive association. Facilities without a treatment adherence rate are excluded from the correlation.

```sql
WITH facility_scores AS (
    SELECT
        fac_key,
        CASE com_res
            WHEN 'Comprehensive' THEN 3
            WHEN 'Extensive' THEN 3
            WHEN 'Adequate' THEN 2
            WHEN 'Limited' THEN 1
        END AS resource_score
    FROM main.facilities
), adherence_by_facility AS (
    SELECT
        e.fac_id AS fac_key,
        CAST(COUNT(*) FILTER (
            WHERE o.txprogmet->>'Tx_Adh' IN ('High', 'Medium', 'Compliant')
        ) AS DOUBLE) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) AS adherence_rate
    FROM main.treatmentoutcomes AS o
    JOIN main.treatmentbasics AS tb ON o.tx_ref = tb.tx_key
    JOIN main.encounters AS e ON tb.enc_ref = e.enc_key
    GROUP BY e.fac_id
), facility_metrics AS (
    SELECT
        fs.fac_key,
        fs.resource_score,
        abf.adherence_rate
    FROM facility_scores AS fs
    LEFT JOIN adherence_by_facility AS abf ON fs.fac_key = abf.fac_key
)
SELECT
    (SELECT AVG(resource_score) FROM facility_metrics) AS overall_resource_adequacy_score,
    (SELECT CORR(resource_score, adherence_rate)
     FROM facility_metrics
     WHERE adherence_rate IS NOT NULL) AS resource_adherence_correlation;
```

answer:
The schema does not define PFIS, FRAI, or RDD as fields or provide formulas for them, so I’ve made their definitions explicit: **PFIS** is the percentage of a facility’s linked assessments rated High or Severe for suicide risk; **FRAI** is a 0–100 average resource-availability index based on support services, community resources, emergency contacts, and safety/crisis plans; **RDD** is PFIS minus FRAI. By this definition, 104 facilities exceed the 20% PFIS threshold, and the query returns the top 100 by RDD.

The first results are F798 (PFIS 100.00, FRAI 15.00, RDD 85.00), F247 (100.00, 26.67, 73.33), and F281 (100.00, 33.33, 66.67).

```sql
WITH facility_assessments AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        e.fac_id,
        e.ab_ref,
        lower(trim(s.suic_risk)) AS suic_risk
    FROM encounters e
    JOIN assessmentsymptomsandrisk s
        ON s.asr_key = e.ab_ref
    WHERE e.fac_id IS NOT NULL
      AND e.ab_ref IS NOT NULL
      AND s.suic_risk IS NOT NULL
),
risk_scores AS (
    SELECT
        fac_id,
        100.0 * count(*) FILTER (
            WHERE suic_risk IN ('high', 'severe')
        ) / NULLIF(count(*), 0) AS pfis
    FROM facility_assessments
    GROUP BY fac_id
),
resource_scores AS (
    SELECT
        f.fac_key,
        100.0 * (
            coalesce(
                CASE
                    WHEN lower(f.spt_svc) LIKE '%comprehensive%' THEN 1.0
                    WHEN lower(f.spt_svc) LIKE '%adequate%' THEN 0.75
                    WHEN lower(f.spt_svc) LIKE '%limited%' THEN 0.25
                    WHEN nullif(trim(f.spt_svc), '') IS NOT NULL THEN 0.5
                END,
                0.0
            )
            + coalesce(
                CASE lower(trim(f.com_res))
                    WHEN 'extensive' THEN 1.0
                    WHEN 'comprehensive' THEN 0.8
                    WHEN 'adequate' THEN 0.6
                    WHEN 'limited' THEN 0.3
                END,
                0.0
            )
            + coalesce(
                least(try_cast(f.emer_contact AS DOUBLE), 10.0) / 10.0,
                0.0
            )
            + coalesce(
                CASE lower(trim(f.s_plan_stat))
                    WHEN 'in place' THEN 1.0
                    WHEN 'active' THEN 1.0
                    WHEN 'needs update' THEN 0.5
                END,
                0.0
            )
            + coalesce(
                CASE lower(trim(f.c_plan_stat))
                    WHEN 'in place' THEN 1.0
                    WHEN 'active' THEN 1.0
                    WHEN 'needs update' THEN 0.5
                END,
                0.0
            )
        ) / NULLIF(
            (CASE WHEN nullif(trim(f.spt_svc), '') IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
            + (CASE WHEN lower(trim(f.com_res)) IN
                ('extensive', 'comprehensive', 'adequate', 'limited')
                THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
            + (CASE WHEN try_cast(f.emer_contact AS DOUBLE) IS NOT NULL
                THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
            + (CASE WHEN lower(trim(f.s_plan_stat)) IN
                ('in place', 'active', 'needs update')
                THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
            + (CASE WHEN lower(trim(f.c_plan_stat)) IN
                ('in place', 'active', 'needs update')
                THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),
            0
        ) AS frai
    FROM facilities f
)
SELECT
    f.fac_key AS facility_id,
    round(r.pfis, 2) AS pfis_score,
    round(rs.frai, 2) AS frai_score,
    round(r.pfis - rs.frai, 2) AS rdd_score
FROM risk_scores r
JOIN facilities f
    ON f.fac_key = r.fac_id
JOIN resource_scores rs
    ON rs.fac_key = f.fac_key
WHERE r.pfis > 20
ORDER BY rdd_score DESC, pfis_score DESC, facility_id
LIMIT 100;
```

    FROM encounters e

        ON s.asr_key = e.ab_ref
    WHERE e.fac_id IS NOT NULL
      AND e.ab_ref IS NOT NULL
      AND s.suic_risk IS NOT NULL
),
risk_scores AS (
    SELECT
        fac_id,
        100.0 * count(*) FILTER (
            WHERE suic_risk IN ('high', 'severe')
        ) / NULLIF(count(*), 0) AS pfis
    FROM facility_assessments
    GROUP BY fac_id
),
resource_scores AS (
    SELECT
        f.fac_key,
        100.0 * (
            coalesce(
                CASE
                    WHEN lower(f.spt_svc) LIKE '%comprehensive%' THEN 1.0
                    WHEN lower(f.spt_svc) LIKE '%adequate%' THEN 0.75
                    WHEN lower(f.spt_svc) LIKE '%limited%' THEN 0.25
                    WHEN nullif(trim(f.spt_svc), '') IS NOT NULL THEN 0.5
                END,
                0.0
            )
            + coalesce(
                CASE lower(trim(f.com_res))
                    WHEN 'extensive' THEN 1.0
                    WHEN 'comprehensive' THEN 0.8
                    WHEN 'adequate' THEN 0.6
                    WHEN 'limited' THEN 0.3
                END,
                0.0
            )
            + coalesce(
                least(try_cast(f.emer_contact AS DOUBLE), 10.0) / 10.0,
                0.0
            )
            + coalesce(
                CASE lower(trim(f.s_plan_stat))
                    WHEN 'in place' THEN 1.0
                    WHEN 'active' THEN 1.0
                    WHEN 'needs update' THEN 0.5
                END,
                0.0
            )
            + coalesce(
                CASE lower(trim(f.c_plan_stat))
                    WHEN 'in place' THEN 1.0
                    WHEN 'active' THEN 1.0
                    WHEN 'needs update' THEN 0.5
                END,
                0.0
            )
        ) / NULLIF(
            (CASE WHEN nullif(trim(f.spt_svc), '') IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
            + (CASE WHEN lower(trim(f.com_res)) IN
                ('extensive', 'comprehensive', 'adequate', 'limited')
                THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
            + (CASE WHEN try_cast(f.emer_contact AS DOUBLE) IS NOT NULL
                THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
            + (CASE WHEN lower(trim(f.s_plan_stat)) IN
                ('in place', 'active', 'needs update')
                THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
            + (CASE WHEN lower(trim(f.c_plan_stat)) IN
                ('in place', 'active', 'needs update')
                THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),
            0
        ) AS frai
    FROM facilities f
)
SELECT
    f.fac_key AS facility_id,
    round(r.pfis, 2) AS pfis_score,
    round(rs.frai, 2) AS frai_score,
    round(r.pfis - rs.frai, 2) AS rdd_score
FROM risk_scores r
JOIN facilities f
    ON f.fac_key = r.fac_id
JOIN resource_scores rs
    ON rs.fac_key = f.fac_key
WHERE r.pfis > 20
ORDER BY rdd_score DESC, pfis_score DESC, facility_id
LIMIT 100;

answer:
The query below returns 100 facilities, sorted by performance quadrant and then facility ID. Quadrants use the median treatment adherence rate and patient stability metric across facilities as their thresholds. Both metrics are rounded to two decimal places.

```sql
WITH encounter_stats AS (
  SELECT
    fac_id AS fac_key,
    SUM(miss_appt) AS missed_appointments,
    COUNT(DISTINCT pat_ref) AS patient_count
  FROM encounters
  GROUP BY fac_id
),
crisis_stats AS (
  SELECT
    e.fac_id AS fac_key,
    SUM(tb.crisis_int) AS crisis_interventions
  FROM encounters e
  JOIN treatmentbasics tb ON tb.enc_ref = e.enc_key
  GROUP BY e.fac_id
),
adherence_stats AS (
  SELECT
    e.fac_id AS fac_key,
    CAST(
      COUNT(*) FILTER (
        WHERE tox.txprogmet->>'Tx_Adh' IN ('High', 'Medium', 'Compliant')
      ) AS DOUBLE
    ) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) AS adherence_rate
  FROM treatmentoutcomes tox
  JOIN treatmentbasics tb ON tox.tx_ref = tb.tx_key
  JOIN encounters e ON tb.enc_ref = e.enc_key
  GROUP BY e.fac_id
),
facility_metrics AS (
  SELECT
    f.fac_key,
    a.adherence_rate,
    1.0 / (
      1.0
      + c.crisis_interventions / NULLIF(es.patient_count, 0)
      + es.missed_appointments / NULLIF(es.patient_count, 0)
    ) AS stability_metric
  FROM facilities f
  LEFT JOIN adherence_stats a ON a.fac_key = f.fac_key
  LEFT JOIN encounter_stats es ON es.fac_key = f.fac_key
  LEFT JOIN crisis_stats c ON c.fac_key = f.fac_key
),
thresholds AS (
  SELECT
    median(adherence_rate) AS median_adherence,
    median(stability_metric) AS median_stability
  FROM facility_metrics
),
classified AS (
  SELECT
    fm.fac_key,
    fm.adherence_rate,
    fm.stability_metric,
    CASE
      WHEN fm.adherence_rate >= t.median_adherence
       AND fm.stability_metric >= t.median_stability
        THEN 'High Adherence / High Stability'
      WHEN fm.adherence_rate >= t.median_adherence
        THEN 'High Adherence / Low Stability'
      WHEN fm.stability_metric >= t.median_stability
        THEN 'Low Adherence / High Stability'
      ELSE 'Low Adherence / Low Stability'
    END AS performance_quadrant
  FROM facility_metrics fm
  CROSS JOIN thresholds t
)
SELECT
  fac_key AS facility_id,
  CAST(ROUND(adherence_rate, 2) AS DECIMAL(10,2)) AS treatment_adherence_rate,
  CAST(ROUND(stability_metric, 2) AS DECIMAL(10,2)) AS patient_stability_metric,
  performance_quadrant
FROM classified
ORDER BY performance_quadrant, facility_id
LIMIT 100;
```

The query includes numeric 2–6 digit NAICS codes and only applications where offered and prevailing wage units match and are recognized. Wages are annualized per the metric definition before calculating the percentage difference.

```sql
WITH application_wages AS (
  SELECT
    c.filekey,
    e.employer_contact_info->>'naics_code' AS naics_code,
    pw.wage_details->'offered_wage'->>'from' AS offered_text,
    pw.wage_details->'offered_wage'->>'unit' AS offered_unit,
    pw.wage_details->'prevailing_wage'->>'value' AS prevailing_text,
    pw.wage_details->'prevailing_wage'->>'unit' AS prevailing_unit
  FROM main.cases AS c
  JOIN main.employer AS e
    ON e.corphandle = c.homefirm AND e.zipref = c.homezip
  JOIN main.case_worksite AS cw
    ON cw.dockkey = c.filekey
  JOIN main.prevailing_wage AS pw
    ON pw.trackno = cw.wagetrack
), parsed AS (
  SELECT
    filekey,
    naics_code,
    TRY_CAST(REPLACE(REPLACE(offered_text, '$', ''), ',', '') AS DOUBLE) AS offered_wage,
    TRY_CAST(REPLACE(REPLACE(prevailing_text, 'USD', ''), ',', '') AS DOUBLE) AS prevailing_wage,
    offered_unit,
    prevailing_unit,
    CASE offered_unit
      WHEN 'Hour' THEN 2080
      WHEN 'Week' THEN 52
      WHEN 'Month' THEN 12
      WHEN 'Year' THEN 1
    END AS annual_factor
  FROM application_wages
)
SELECT
  naics_code,
  COUNT(DISTINCT filekey) AS application_count,
  ROUND(
    AVG(
      ((offered_wage * annual_factor - prevailing_wage * annual_factor)
        / (prevailing_wage * annual_factor)) * 100
    ),
    2
  ) AS avg_industry_wage_difference
FROM parsed
WHERE regexp_full_match(naics_code, '[0-9]{2,6}')
  AND offered_wage IS NOT NULL
  AND prevailing_wage > 0
  AND offered_unit = prevailing_unit
  AND offered_unit IN ('Hour', 'Week', 'Month', 'Year')
GROUP BY naics_code
ORDER BY avg_industry_wage_difference DESC
LIMIT 5
```

answer:
The Patient Stability Metric is facility-level, so clinicians at the same facility share the same score and tie in the within-facility ranking. The query excludes resource-backed facilities where the metric is unavailable.

```sql
WITH facility_psm AS (
    SELECT
        f.fac_key,
        1.0 / (
            1 + (SELECT SUM(tb.crisis_int)
                 FROM main.encounters e
                 JOIN main.treatmentbasics tb ON tb.enc_ref = e.enc_key
                 WHERE e.fac_id = f.fac_key) * 1.0
                / (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT e2.pat_ref)
                   FROM main.encounters e2
                   WHERE e2.fac_id = f.fac_key)
              + (SELECT SUM(e3.miss_appt) / COUNT(DISTINCT e3.pat_ref)
                 FROM main.encounters e3
                 WHERE e3.fac_id = f.fac_key)
        ) AS patient_stability_metric_score
    FROM main.facilities f
    WHERE f.com_res IN ('Adequate', 'Comprehensive', 'Extensive')
),
clinician_ranked AS (
    SELECT
        c.clin_key AS clinician_id,
        c.fac_connect AS facility_id,
        fp.patient_stability_metric_score,
        RANK() OVER (
            PARTITION BY c.fac_connect
            ORDER BY fp.patient_stability_metric_score DESC
        ) AS facility_rank
    FROM main.clinicians c
    JOIN facility_psm fp ON fp.fac_key = c.fac_connect
    WHERE fp.patient_stability_metric_score IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
    clinician_id,
    facility_id,
    patient_stability_metric_score,
    facility_rank
FROM clinician_ranked
ORDER BY facility_id, facility_rank
LIMIT 100
```

I treated **resource-demand differential** as an index: the facility’s environmental-stress and life-impact scores (each scored mild = 1, moderate = 2, severe = 3) minus its community-resource and support-service scores. Higher differentials indicate more recorded stress relative to documented resources. Facilities with no recorded environmental or life-impact stress are excluded. The query was run and returns the top 100 by that measure.

```sql
WITH scored AS (
  SELECT
    fac_key,
    (
      CASE lower(env_stress)
        WHEN 'mild' THEN 1
        WHEN 'moderate' THEN 2
        WHEN 'severe' THEN 3
        ELSE 0
      END
      +
      CASE lower(life_impact)
        WHEN 'mild' THEN 1
        WHEN 'moderate' THEN 2
        WHEN 'severe' THEN 3
        ELSE 0
      END
    ) AS demand_score,
    (
      CASE lower(com_res)
        WHEN 'limited' THEN 1
        WHEN 'adequate' THEN 2
        WHEN 'comprehensive' THEN 3
        WHEN 'extensive' THEN 3
        ELSE 0
      END
      +
      CASE
        WHEN lower(coalesce(spt_svc, '')) LIKE '%comprehensive%' THEN 3
        WHEN lower(coalesce(spt_svc, '')) LIKE '%adequate%' THEN 2
        WHEN lower(coalesce(spt_svc, '')) LIKE '%limited%' THEN 1
        ELSE least(
          CASE WHEN lower(coalesce(spt_svc, '')) LIKE '%case management%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
          + CASE WHEN lower(coalesce(spt_svc, '')) LIKE '%employment%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
          + CASE WHEN lower(coalesce(spt_svc, '')) LIKE '%housing%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
          + CASE WHEN lower(coalesce(spt_svc, '')) LIKE '%legal%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END,
          3
        )
      END
    ) AS resource_score
  FROM facilities
),
differentials AS (
  SELECT
    fac_key,
    demand_score - resource_score AS resource_demand_differential,
    demand_score
  FROM scored
  WHERE demand_score > 0
)
SELECT
  fac_key AS facility_id,
  resource_demand_differential
FROM differentials
ORDER BY resource_demand_differential DESC, demand_score DESC, facility_id
LIMIT 100;
```

answer:
I used the governed treatment-adherence rate and patient-stability metric. Quadrants are based on whether each metric is at or above its average across facilities; the top 100 are ranked by the sum of the two metrics, with adherence and stability as tie-breakers. The query ran successfully and returns up to 100 facilities with non-NULL values for both metrics.

```sql
WITH facility_metrics AS (
    SELECT
        facilities.fac_key AS facility_id,
        (
            SELECT CAST(
                COUNT(*) FILTER (
                    WHERE o.txprogmet->>'Tx_Adh' IN ('High', 'Medium', 'Compliant')
                ) AS DOUBLE PRECISION
            ) / COUNT(*)
            FROM main.treatmentoutcomes o
            JOIN main.treatmentbasics tb ON o.tx_ref = tb.tx_key
            JOIN main.encounters e ON tb.enc_ref = e.enc_key
            WHERE e.fac_id = facilities.fac_key
        ) AS adherence_rate,
        1.0 / (
            1
            + (
                SELECT SUM(tb.crisis_int)
                FROM main.encounters e
                JOIN main.treatmentbasics tb ON tb.enc_ref = e.enc_key
                WHERE e.fac_id = facilities.fac_key
            ) * 1.0 / (
                SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT e2.pat_ref)
                FROM main.encounters e2
                WHERE e2.fac_id = facilities.fac_key
            )
            + (
                SELECT SUM(e3.miss_appt) / COUNT(DISTINCT e3.pat_ref)
                FROM main.encounters e3
                WHERE e3.fac_id = facilities.fac_key
            )
        ) AS stability
    FROM main.facilities
),
benchmarks AS (
    SELECT
        AVG(adherence_rate) AS avg_adherence,
        AVG(stability) AS avg_stability
    FROM facility_metrics
),
classified AS (
    SELECT
        fm.facility_id,
        fm.adherence_rate,
        fm.stability,
        CASE
            WHEN fm.adherence_rate >= b.avg_adherence
             AND fm.stability >= b.avg_stability
                THEN 'High adherence / High stability'
            WHEN fm.adherence_rate >= b.avg_adherence
             AND fm.stability < b.avg_stability
                THEN 'High adherence / Low stability'
            WHEN fm.adherence_rate < b.avg_adherence
             AND fm.stability >= b.avg_stability
                THEN 'Low adherence / High stability'
            ELSE 'Low adherence / Low stability'
        END AS quadrant,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            ORDER BY
                fm.adherence_rate + fm.stability DESC,
                fm.adherence_rate DESC,
                fm.stability DESC,
                fm.facility_id
        ) AS performance_rank
    FROM facility_metrics fm
    CROSS JOIN benchmarks b
    WHERE fm.adherence_rate IS NOT NULL
      AND fm.stability IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
    facility_id,
    ROUND(adherence_rate, 2) AS treatment_adherence_rate,
    ROUND(stability, 2) AS patient_stability,
    quadrant
FROM classified
WHERE performance_rank <= 100
ORDER BY quadrant, facility_id;
```

```sql
    GROUP BY fa.fac_id

            END
        ) AS pfis_score
    FROM facility_assessments AS fa

    GROUP BY fa.fac_id
),
facility_scores AS (
    SELECT

        i.pfis_score,

)
```

```sql
WITH
facility_resources AS (
    SELECT
        fac_key,
        CASE lower(com_res)
            WHEN 'comprehensive' THEN 3
            WHEN 'extensive' THEN 3
            WHEN 'adequate' THEN 2
            WHEN 'limited' THEN 1
        END AS frai
    FROM facilities
),
impairment AS (
    SELECT
        e.fac_id,
        AVG(
            CASE lower(s.func_imp)
                WHEN 'severe' THEN 3
                WHEN 'moderate' THEN 2
                WHEN 'mild' THEN 1
            END
        ) AS pfis
    FROM encounters e
    JOIN assessmentsocialanddiagnosis s ON s.asd_key = e.ab_ref
    WHERE s.func_imp IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY e.fac_id
),
engagement AS (
    SELECT
        e.fac_id,
        AVG(
            CASE lower(t.th_eng)
                WHEN 'high' THEN 3
                WHEN 'medium' THEN 2
                WHEN 'low' THEN 1
            END
        ) AS tes
    FROM encounters e
    JOIN treatmentbasics t ON t.enc_ref = e.enc_key
    WHERE t.th_eng IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY e.fac_id
),
adherence AS (
    SELECT
        e.fac_id,
        AVG(
            CASE
                WHEN lower(o.txprogmet ->> 'Tx_Adh') IN ('high', 'medium', 'compliant')
                THEN 1.0
                ELSE 0.0
            END
        ) AS tar
    FROM encounters e
    JOIN treatmentbasics t ON t.enc_ref = e.enc_key
    JOIN treatmentoutcomes o ON o.tx_ref = t.tx_key
    GROUP BY e.fac_id
),
attendance AS (
    SELECT
        fac_id,
        SUM(miss_appt) / COUNT(DISTINCT pat_ref) AS mar
    FROM encounters
    GROUP BY fac_id
)
SELECT
    r.fac_key AS facility_id,
    i.pfis - r.frai AS resource_demand_differential
FROM facility_resources r
JOIN impairment i ON i.fac_id = r.fac_key
JOIN engagement g ON g.fac_id = r.fac_key
JOIN adherence a ON a.fac_id = r.fac_key
JOIN attendance m ON m.fac_id = r.fac_key
WHERE i.pfis - r.frai > 1.0
  AND (g.tes + a.tar * 3) / 2 < 1.5
  AND m.mar > 2.5
ORDER BY resource_demand_differential DESC, facility_id
LIMIT 100;
```

Only one facility meets the systemic-stress criteria: **F766**, with a resource-demand differential of **2.0**.

```sql
WITH resource AS (
  SELECT fac_key,
         CASE com_res
           WHEN 'Comprehensive' THEN 3
           WHEN 'Extensive' THEN 3
           WHEN 'Adequate' THEN 2
           WHEN 'Limited' THEN 1
         END AS frai
  FROM facilities
),
pfis AS (
  SELECT e.fac_id,
         AVG(CASE UPPER(asd.func_imp)
               WHEN 'SEVERE' THEN 3
               WHEN 'MODERATE' THEN 2
               WHEN 'MILD' THEN 1
             END) AS pfis
  FROM assessmentsocialanddiagnosis AS asd
  JOIN assessmentbasics AS ab ON ab.ab_key = asd.asd_key
  JOIN patients AS p ON p.pat_key = ab.pat_owner_ref
  JOIN encounters AS e ON e.pat_ref = p.pat_key
  GROUP BY e.fac_id
),
tes AS (
  SELECT e.fac_id,
         AVG(CASE tb.th_eng
               WHEN 'High' THEN 3
               WHEN 'Medium' THEN 2
               WHEN 'Low' THEN 1
             END) AS tes
  FROM treatmentbasics AS tb
  JOIN encounters AS e ON e.enc_key = tb.enc_ref
  GROUP BY e.fac_id
),
tar AS (
  SELECT e.fac_id,
         COUNT(*) FILTER (
           WHERE o.txprogmet->>'Tx_Adh' IN ('High', 'Medium', 'Compliant')
         )::DOUBLE / COUNT(*) AS tar
  FROM treatmentoutcomes AS o
  JOIN treatmentbasics AS tb ON tb.tx_key = o.tx_ref
  JOIN encounters AS e ON e.enc_key = tb.enc_ref
  GROUP BY e.fac_id
),
mar AS (
  SELECT fac_id,
         SUM(miss_appt) / COUNT(DISTINCT pat_ref) AS mar
  FROM encounters
  GROUP BY fac_id
),
metrics AS (
  SELECT r.fac_key,
         p.pfis - r.frai AS resource_demand_differential,
         (t.tes + a.tar * 3) / 2 AS eas,
         m.mar
  FROM resource AS r
  LEFT JOIN pfis AS p ON p.fac_id = r.fac_key
  LEFT JOIN tes AS t ON t.fac_id = r.fac_key
  LEFT JOIN tar AS a ON a.fac_id = r.fac_key
  LEFT JOIN mar AS m ON m.fac_id = r.fac_key
)
SELECT fac_key AS facility_id,
       resource_demand_differential
FROM metrics
WHERE resource_demand_differential > 1.0
  AND eas < 1.5
  AND mar > 2.5
ORDER BY resource_demand_differential DESC, facility_id
LIMIT 100;
```

answer:
This returns one row per patient, with PHQ-9 and GAD-7 averages across their linked symptom assessments and a mean treatment-adherence score across their recorded outcomes. The adherence score is ordinal: 1 = non-compliant, 2 = low, 3 = medium, 4 = high, 5 = compliant. The final row is the all-patient baseline; ethnicity groups are alphabetical, with that summary row last. Missing data remains `NULL`.

```sql
WITH patient_symptoms AS (
    SELECT
        ab.pat_owner_ref AS pat_key,
        AVG(asr.phq9_scr) AS avg_phq9_score,
        AVG(asr.gad7_scr) AS avg_gad7_score,
        COUNT(DISTINCT ab.ab_key) AS symptom_assessments
    FROM assessmentbasics ab
    JOIN assessmentsymptomsandrisk asr
        ON asr.asr_key = ab.ab_key
    WHERE ab.pat_owner_ref IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY ab.pat_owner_ref
),
patient_adherence AS (
    SELECT
        e.pat_ref AS pat_key,
        AVG(
            CASE lower(trim(outc.txprogmet ->> 'Tx_Adh'))
                WHEN 'non-compliant' THEN 1.0
                WHEN 'low' THEN 2.0
                WHEN 'medium' THEN 3.0
                WHEN 'high' THEN 4.0
                WHEN 'compliant' THEN 5.0
            END
        ) AS avg_treatment_adherence_score,
        COUNT(*) FILTER (
            WHERE outc.txprogmet ->> 'Tx_Adh' IS NOT NULL
        ) AS adherence_observations
    FROM treatmentoutcomes outc
    JOIN treatmentbasics tb
        ON tb.tx_key = outc.tx_ref
    JOIN encounters e
        ON e.enc_key = tb.enc_ref
    WHERE e.pat_ref IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY e.pat_ref
),
patient_metrics AS (
    SELECT
        p.pat_key,
        p.pat_eth AS ethnicity,
        ps.avg_phq9_score,
        ps.avg_gad7_score,
        ps.symptom_assessments,
        pa.avg_treatment_adherence_score,
        pa.adherence_observations
    FROM patients p
    LEFT JOIN patient_symptoms ps
        ON ps.pat_key = p.pat_key
    LEFT JOIN patient_adherence pa
        ON pa.pat_key = p.pat_key
),
report AS (
    SELECT
        ethnicity,
        pat_key AS patient_key,
        1 AS patients_in_row,
        avg_phq9_score,
        avg_gad7_score,
        avg_treatment_adherence_score,
        symptom_assessments,
        adherence_observations,
        0 AS sort_order
    FROM patient_metrics

    UNION ALL

    SELECT
        'All Ethnicities' AS ethnicity,
        NULL AS patient_key,
        COUNT(*) AS patients_in_row,
        AVG(avg_phq9_score) AS avg_phq9_score,
        AVG(avg_gad7_score) AS avg_gad7_score,
        AVG(avg_treatment_adherence_score) AS avg_treatment_adherence_score,
        SUM(symptom_assessments) AS symptom_assessments,
        SUM(adherence_observations) AS adherence_observations,
        1 AS sort_order
    FROM patient_metrics
)
SELECT
    ethnicity,
    patient_key,
    patients_in_row,
    avg_phq9_score,
    avg_gad7_score,
    avg_treatment_adherence_score,
    symptom_assessments,
    adherence_observations
FROM report
ORDER BY sort_order, ethnicity, patient_key;
```

- **Expected annual quality-of-life gain:** $1,200 × 0.0509 = **61.08 points** — **above** the 50-point good-value threshold.

```sql
WITH ranked AS (
  SELECT
    p.pat_key AS patient_id,
    e.enc_key,

    a.ab_key AS assessment_id,

      regexp_extract(a.therapy_exp_intensity, '([0-9]+(?:\\.[0-9]+)?)', 1)
      AS DOUBLE
    ) AS therapy_hours_per_month,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY p.pat_key

  FROM patients p
  JOIN encounters e ON e.pat_ref = p.pat_key
  JOIN assessmentbasics a ON a.ab_key = e.ab_ref
  WHERE p.pat_key = 'P883117'
)
SELECT

  enc_key,
  time_mark,
  a_type,
  therapy_exp_intensity,
  therapy_hours_per_month >= 5 AS meets_5_hour_target,
  0.0509 AS cost_effectiveness_rate_qol_per_dollar,
  1200 AS annual_budget_dollars,
```

Only one facility meets the systemic-stress criteria:

| Facility ID | Resource-demand differential |
|---|---:|
| F766 | 2.0 |

```sql
WITH facility_metrics AS (
  SELECT
    f.fac_key,
    (
      (SELECT AVG(CASE UPPER(asd.func_imp) WHEN 'SEVERE' THEN 3 WHEN 'MODERATE' THEN 2 WHEN 'MILD' THEN 1 END)
       FROM main.assessmentsocialanddiagnosis AS asd
       JOIN main.assessmentbasics AS ab ON asd.asd_key = ab.ab_key
       JOIN main.patients AS p ON ab.pat_owner_ref = p.pat_key
       JOIN main.encounters AS e ON e.pat_ref = p.pat_key
       WHERE e.fac_id = f.fac_key)
      - CASE f.com_res
          WHEN 'Comprehensive' THEN 3
          WHEN 'Extensive' THEN 3
          WHEN 'Adequate' THEN 2
          WHEN 'Limited' THEN 1
        END
    ) AS resource_demand_differential,
    (
      (
        (SELECT AVG(CASE tb.th_eng WHEN 'High' THEN 3 WHEN 'Medium' THEN 2 WHEN 'Low' THEN 1 END)
         FROM main.treatmentbasics AS tb
         JOIN main.encounters AS e ON tb.enc_ref = e.enc_key
         WHERE e.fac_id = f.fac_key)
        +
        (SELECT CAST(COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE o.txprogmet->>'Tx_Adh' IN ('High', 'Medium', 'Compliant')) AS DOUBLE) / COUNT(*)
         FROM main.treatmentoutcomes AS o
         JOIN main.treatmentbasics AS tb ON o.tx_ref = tb.tx_key
         JOIN main.encounters AS e ON tb.enc_ref = e.enc_key
         WHERE e.fac_id = f.fac_key) * 3
      ) / 2
    ) AS engagement_adherence_score,
    (SELECT SUM(e.miss_appt) / COUNT(DISTINCT e.pat_ref)
     FROM main.encounters AS e
     WHERE e.fac_id = f.fac_key) AS missed_appointment_rate
  FROM main.facilities AS f
)
SELECT fac_key, resource_demand_differential
FROM facility_metrics
WHERE resource_demand_differential > 1.0
  AND engagement_adherence_score < 1.5
  AND missed_appointment_rate > 2.5
ORDER BY resource_demand_differential DESC, fac_key
LIMIT 100;
```

answer:
This returns one row per patient, with their average PHQ-9 and GAD-7 scores across linked assessments, severity bands, and the percentage of recorded treatment outcomes rated High, Medium, or Compliant for adherence. The final row is the all-patient baseline; ethnicities are sorted alphabetically.

```sql
WITH assessment_by_patient AS (
    SELECT
        ab.pat_owner_ref AS pat_key,
        AVG(asr.phq9_scr) AS avg_phq9,
        AVG(asr.gad7_scr) AS avg_gad7
    FROM assessmentbasics ab
    LEFT JOIN assessmentsymptomsandrisk AS asr
        ON asr.asr_key = ab.ab_key
    WHERE ab.pat_owner_ref IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY ab.pat_owner_ref
),
adherence_by_patient AS (
    SELECT
        e.pat_ref AS pat_key,
        100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (
            WHERE LOWER(json_extract_string(o.txprogmet, '$.Tx_Adh'))
                IN ('high', 'medium', 'compliant')
        )
        / NULLIF(
            COUNT(*) FILTER (
                WHERE json_extract_string(o.txprogmet, '$.Tx_Adh') IS NOT NULL
            ),
            0
        ) AS adherence_pct
    FROM treatmentbasics t
    JOIN encounters e
        ON e.enc_key = t.enc_ref
    JOIN treatmentoutcomes o
        ON o.tx_ref = t.tx_key
    WHERE e.pat_ref IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY e.pat_ref
),
patient_metrics AS (
    SELECT
        p.pat_key,
        p.pat_eth,
        a.avg_phq9,
        a.avg_gad7,
        ad.adherence_pct
    FROM patients p
    LEFT JOIN assessment_by_patient a
        ON a.pat_key = p.pat_key
    LEFT JOIN adherence_by_patient ad
        ON ad.pat_key = p.pat_key
),
report AS (
    SELECT
        pat_key AS patient_id,
        pat_eth AS ethnicity,
        1 AS patient_count,
        ROUND(avg_phq9, 2) AS avg_phq9_score,
        CASE
            WHEN avg_phq9 IS NULL THEN NULL
            WHEN avg_phq9 < 5 THEN 'Minimal'
            WHEN avg_phq9 < 10 THEN 'Mild'
            WHEN avg_phq9 < 15 THEN 'Moderate'
            WHEN avg_phq9 < 20 THEN 'Moderately Severe'
            ELSE 'Severe'
        END AS phq9_severity,
        ROUND(avg_gad7, 2) AS avg_gad7_score,
        CASE
            WHEN avg_gad7 IS NULL THEN NULL
            WHEN avg_gad7 < 5 THEN 'Minimal'
            WHEN avg_gad7 < 10 THEN 'Mild'
            WHEN avg_gad7 < 15 THEN 'Moderate'
            ELSE 'Severe'
        END AS gad7_severity,
        ROUND(adherence_pct, 2) AS treatment_adherence_pct
    FROM patient_metrics

    UNION ALL

    SELECT
        'ALL PATIENTS',
        'All Ethnicities',
        COUNT(*),
        ROUND(AVG(avg_phq9), 2),
        CASE
            WHEN AVG(avg_phq9) IS NULL THEN NULL
            WHEN AVG(avg_phq9) < 5 THEN 'Minimal'
            WHEN AVG(avg_phq9) < 10 THEN 'Mild'
            WHEN AVG(avg_phq9) < 15 THEN 'Moderate'
            WHEN AVG(avg_phq9) < 20 THEN 'Moderately Severe'
            ELSE 'Severe'
        END,
        ROUND(AVG(avg_gad7), 2),
        CASE
            WHEN AVG(avg_gad7) IS NULL THEN NULL
            WHEN AVG(avg_gad7) < 5 THEN 'Minimal'
            WHEN AVG(avg_gad7) < 10 THEN 'Mild'
            WHEN AVG(avg_gad7) < 15 THEN 'Moderate'
            ELSE 'Severe'
        END,
        ROUND(AVG(adherence_pct), 2)
    FROM patient_metrics
)
SELECT *
FROM report
ORDER BY
    CASE WHEN ethnicity = 'All Ethnicities' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END,
    ethnicity,
    patient_id;
```

WITH srp AS (
    SELECT
        e.fac_id,
        100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE r.suic_risk = 'High') / COUNT(*) AS suicide_risk_pct
    FROM encounters e
    JOIN assessmentsymptomsandrisk r
        ON r.asr_key = e.ab_ref
    GROUP BY e.fac_id
),
pfis AS (
    SELECT
        e.fac_id,
        AVG(
            CASE UPPER(asd.func_imp)
                WHEN 'SEVERE' THEN 3
                WHEN 'MODERATE' THEN 2
                WHEN 'MILD' THEN 1
            END
        ) AS pfis
    FROM assessmentsocialanddiagnosis asd
    JOIN assessmentbasics ab
        ON ab.ab_key = asd.asd_key
    JOIN patients p
        ON p.pat_key = ab.pat_owner_ref
    JOIN encounters e
        ON e.pat_ref = p.pat_key
    GROUP BY e.fac_id
),
scored AS (
    SELECT
        f.fac_key AS facility_id,
        p.pfis,
        CASE f.com_res
            WHEN 'Comprehensive' THEN 3
            WHEN 'Extensive' THEN 3
            WHEN 'Adequate' THEN 2
            WHEN 'Limited' THEN 1
        END AS frai
    FROM facilities f
    JOIN srp s
        ON s.fac_id = f.fac_key
    LEFT JOIN pfis p
        ON p.fac_id = f.fac_key
    WHERE s.suicide_risk_pct > 20
)
SELECT
    facility_id,
    pfis,
    frai,
    pfis - frai AS rdd
FROM scored
ORDER BY rdd DESC NULLS LAST, facility_id
LIMIT 100;

answer:
- **Patient:** P883117
- **Therapy intensity:** The latest encounter timestamp is tied across two assessments: **4.8 hours/month** (below the 5-hour target) and **6.13 hours/month** (meeting it). The records therefore don’t give a single unambiguous answer.
- **Expected annual QoL gain:** 0.0509 × $1,200 = **61.08 points**.
- **Over the 50-point threshold?** **Yes**, by 11.08 points.

```sql
WITH latest_time AS (
  SELECT MAX(e.time_mark) AS time_mark
  FROM encounters e
  WHERE e.pat_ref = 'P883117'
),
latest_assessments AS (
  SELECT
    e.enc_key,
    e.time_mark,
    ab.ab_key,
    ab.therapy_exp_intensity,
    TRY_CAST(
      regexp_extract(ab.therapy_exp_intensity, '^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?', 1)
      AS DOUBLE
    ) AS therapy_hours
  FROM encounters e
  JOIN assessmentbasics ab
    ON ab.ab_key = e.ab_ref
  JOIN latest_time lt
    ON e.time_mark = lt.time_mark
  WHERE e.pat_ref = 'P883117'
)
SELECT
  'P883117' AS patient_id,
  string_agg(
    enc_key || ' / ' || ab_key || ': ' ||
    COALESCE(therapy_exp_intensity, 'not recorded'),
    '; ' ORDER BY enc_key
  ) AS latest_timestamp_assessments,
  CASE
    WHEN bool_and(therapy_hours >= 5) THEN 'Yes'
    WHEN bool_and(therapy_hours < 5) THEN 'No'
    ELSE 'Ambiguous: tied latest assessments disagree'
  END AS meets_5_hours_monthly,
  0.0509 AS cost_effectiveness_rate_qol_points_per_dollar,
  0.0509 * 1200 AS expected_annual_qol_gain_points,
  (0.0509 * 1200) > 50 AS exceeds_50_point_threshold
FROM latest_assessments;
```

answer:
At **£100 per hour** and **$1.25 per £1**, the $6,000 annual budget converts to **£4,800**, enough for **48 therapy hours per year**.

The chart records **29.87 hours per month** against a **30-hour monthly target**. He is **not quite meeting it**—the gap is about **0.13 hours per month** (roughly 8 minutes).

Using the stated rate of **0.1197 QoL points per dollar**, spending the full budget corresponds to a potential gain of **718.2 QoL points**, which is **68.2 points above** the 650 benchmark. The exact rate stored in his chart is 0.119760479…, which would imply 718.56 points.

One audit caveat: his chart lists Medicaid coverage as **Pending**, so the assumed $6,000 budget may need confirmation.

```sql
WITH patient_audit AS (
  SELECT
    p.pat_key,
    p.insur_type,
    p.insur_stat,
    TRY_CAST(regexp_extract(a.therapy_exp_intensity, '^[0-9.]+') AS DOUBLE) AS chart_hours_per_month,
    TRY_CAST(regexp_extract(a.treatment_cost_eff, '^[0-9.]+') AS DOUBLE) AS chart_qol_per_dollar
  FROM patients p
  JOIN assessmentbasics a ON a.pat_owner_ref = p.pat_key
  WHERE p.pat_key = 'P425079'
)
SELECT
  pat_key,
  insur_type,
  insur_stat,
  6000.0 AS annual_budget_usd,
  1.25 AS usd_per_gbp,
  100.0 AS gbp_per_therapy_hour,
  6000.0 / 1.25 / 100.0 AS affordable_therapy_hours_per_year,
  chart_hours_per_month,
  30.0 AS target_hours_per_month,
  chart_hours_per_month >= 30.0 AS meets_monthly_target,
  6000.0 * 0.1197 AS potential_qol_gain_using_stated_rate,
  (6000.0 * 0.1197) > 650.0 AS exceeds_650_benchmark,
  chart_qol_per_dollar,
  6000.0 * chart_qol_per_dollar AS potential_qol_gain_using_exact_chart_rate
FROM patient_audit;
```

The report has one row per patient, with their ethnicity and average PHQ-9 and GAD-7 scores across recorded assessments, plus their treatment-adherence rate across recorded outcomes. Adherence counts `High`, `Medium`, or `Compliant` as adherent. The “All ethnicities” row is the average of the patient-level metrics, so each patient contributes equally; missing metrics are excluded from the averages. Results are sorted alphabetically by ethnicity, with the summary row first.

```sql
WITH assessment_metrics AS (
    SELECT
        ab.pat_owner_ref AS pat_key,
        AVG(asr.phq9_scr) AS avg_phq9_score,
        AVG(asr.gad7_scr) AS avg_gad7_score
    FROM assessmentbasics ab
    JOIN assessmentsymptomsandrisk asr
        ON asr.asr_key = ab.ab_key
    GROUP BY ab.pat_owner_ref
),
adherence_metrics AS (
    SELECT
        e.pat_ref AS pat_key,
        100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (
            WHERE txo.txprogmet->>'Tx_Adh' IN ('High', 'Medium', 'Compliant')
        ) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) AS treatment_adherence_rate_pct
    FROM encounters e
    JOIN treatmentbasics tb
        ON tb.enc_ref = e.enc_key
    JOIN treatmentoutcomes txo
        ON txo.tx_ref = tb.tx_key
    GROUP BY e.pat_ref
),
patient_report AS (
    SELECT
        p.pat_key,
        p.pat_eth AS ethnicity,
        am.avg_phq9_score,
        am.avg_gad7_score,
        adm.treatment_adherence_rate_pct
    FROM patients p
    LEFT JOIN assessment_metrics am
        ON am.pat_key = p.pat_key
    LEFT JOIN adherence_metrics adm
        ON adm.pat_key = p.pat_key
)
SELECT
    pat_key,
    ethnicity,
    avg_phq9_score,
    avg_gad7_score,
    treatment_adherence_rate_pct
FROM patient_report

UNION ALL

SELECT
```

The report returns one row per patient, with average PHQ-9 and GAD-7 scores across their recorded assessments and their share of treatment outcomes rated High, Medium, or Compliant. The final row is the all-ethnicity baseline; patients without recorded scores or outcomes have NULLs for those measures.

```sql
WITH symptom_by_patient AS (
    SELECT
        ab.pat_owner_ref AS pat_key,
        AVG(asr.phq9_scr) AS avg_phq9_score,
        AVG(asr.gad7_scr) AS avg_gad7_score
    FROM main.assessmentbasics AS ab
    JOIN main.assessmentsymptomsandrisk AS asr
        ON asr.asr_key = ab.ab_key
    GROUP BY ab.pat_owner_ref
),
adherence_by_patient AS (
    SELECT
        e.pat_ref AS pat_key,
        COUNT(*) FILTER (
            WHERE (o.txprogmet ->> 'Tx_Adh') IN ('High', 'Medium', 'Compliant')
        ) AS adherent_outcomes,
        COUNT(*) AS total_outcomes
    FROM main.treatmentoutcomes AS o
    JOIN main.treatmentbasics AS tb
        ON o.tx_ref = tb.tx_key
    JOIN main.encounters AS e
        ON tb.enc_ref = e.enc_key
    GROUP BY e.pat_ref
),
patient_rows AS (
    SELECT
        p.pat_key,
        p.pat_eth AS ethnicity,

        s.avg_gad7_score,

        a.adherent_outcomes,
```
